subject: good fit indices, but high SRMR in CFA

messages.author: b1357bdd8639a59d
messages.subject: good fit indices, but high SRMR in CFA
parts: I am currently using SEM and CFA on a model with 5 latent factors consisting of 6 variables each. When I run the analysis I get CFI =.901, RMSEA, .062, with a chi-square of 845.88 (p< .001) and a SRMR on .098. Do you have any idea why the SRMR is so large? I have a sample of 301 and the degrees of freedom is 394. And is this a good model fit?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: good fit indices, but high SRMR in CFA
parts: SRMR on .098. Do you have any idea why the SRMR is so large?

For local indicators of misfit (i.e., specific aspects of the data that your model fails to adequately reproduce), use the lavResiduals() function.  The SRMR is just the average of standardized residuals, so it is not very informative about why your model has mediocre fit.  It is almost 0.1, so on average, your model predicts correlations to be about 0.1 different than they actually are.  But there could be many small differences and either a few large ones or only 1-2 very large ones.  That is why you want to look at the actual standardized residuals (for a similar reason you would be curious about pairwise comparisons following a significant omnibus F statistic in ANOVA).
And is this a good model fit?

That is not a question with a single answer.  In what ways does your model fit adequately, and in what was does it fit poorly?  Different indices express model fit in different ways, exposing different aspects of model misfit.  Here's a link to a recent SEMNET post wherein Keith provided a nice analogy.
